title: Seed feature names from the wagon's produce/consume artifact as {verb}-{object}

facts.note: Planning task mentions creating or naming a feature for a wagon.
Planner artifacts (wagon/feature YAML or plan docs) being authored.
Needs a diff-level observer that detects a new or renamed feature entry in a wagon plan.
Whether the agent is in planner role authoring wagons/features is judged from task context.

fires: Planner adds a new feature to a wagon whose produce/consume lists artifacts
Planner renames an existing feature in a wagon plan
doesNotFire: Coder implements an already-named feature without changing its name
Editing a feature's acceptances or description without touching its name
Naming artifacts themselves (covered by artifact naming conventions)

given: A planner is authoring or renaming a feature in a wagon that has produce/consume artifacts
then: Derive the name from a produce/consume artifact (the feature seed) as kebab-case {verb}-{object}, where the verb comes from the artifact type's verb list and the object from the artifact's domain or resource.
prefer: Step 1: identify the seed artifact from the wagon's produce/consume entries
Step 2: classify the artifact type as event, state, data or config
Step 3: select the verb from that type's verb list (the lists are defined by convention planner.feature.verb-selection-by-artifact-type)
Step 4: choose the object from the artifact's domain OR its resource (either is allowed; see examples)
Data example (object from resource): mechanic:decision.choice (data) -> make-choice
State example (object from resource): mechanic:timebank.remaining (state) -> track-timebank
Event example (object from domain): match:started (event) -> start-match
avoid: Inventing feature names not traceable to any produce/consume artifact
Using a verb outside the list for the artifact's type
why: Seeding names from produce/consume artifacts keeps features traceable to the wagon's contract and gives consistent, predictable verb-object names (also used as the feature URN segment).
evidence: Each feature name maps to an artifact in its wagon's produce/consume list
The verb belongs to the verb list for that artifact's type (event/state/data/config) and the object matches the artifact's domain or resource
verifier_detail: Reference mappings: 'mechanic:decision.choice (data) -> make-choice'; 'mechanic:timebank.remaining (state) -> track-timebank'; 'match:started (event) -> start-match'. Object may be taken from either the domain (match) or the resource (choice, timebank).
Term feature_seed: the produce/consume artifact a feature name is derived from.
Artifact types: event, state, data, config; verb lists per type are defined by planner.feature.verb-selection-by-artifact-type.
The source gives no criterion for choosing among several produce/consume artifacts or between domain and resource as object; any choice satisfying the steps is compliant.
